questions.q: What does ITIL 4 Foundation cover, and what is its role in the certification scheme?
options: A narrow deep-dive into change enablement only
The broad scope this course has taught (dimensions, SVS, value chain, practices); it's the required prerequisite for every other ITIL 4 credential
A hands-on ServiceNow administration exam
An optional credential with no prerequisite relationship to anything else
questions.explain: Foundation is intentionally broad and shallow, giving everyone a shared vocabulary, and must be earned before any other ITIL 4 certification.

questions.q: Which stream is built for people who design, deliver, and support IT-enabled services day to day?
options: Strategic Leader (SL)
ITIL 4 Master
Managing Professional (MP)
There is no stream focused on day-to-day service delivery
questions.explain: MP modules go deeper into the practices and value-chain activities this course introduced at a conceptual level.

questions.q: Which module is shared between the Managing Professional and Strategic Leader streams?
options: High Velocity IT
Digital & IT Strategy
Create, Deliver & Support
Direct, Plan & Improve
questions.explain: Direct, Plan & Improve is a required prerequisite shared by both streams, covering governance, strategy, and continual improvement.

questions.q: What is required to earn ITIL 4 Master?
options: Passing the Foundation exam a second time
Holding both the Managing Professional and Strategic Leader designations, plus demonstrating practical application of ITIL concepts at work
Completing High Velocity IT alone
No additional exams beyond Foundation
questions.explain: Master sits above both streams and isn't earned by an exam alone — it also requires demonstrated real-world application.

questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid stating a specific pass percentage or question count for ITIL exams?
options: Because ITIL exams have no defined format at all
Because those specifics can change and are owned by the accrediting bodies; stating an unverified number risks teaching something wrong
Because the exams are entirely open-ended essays
Because PeopleCert refuses to publish any exam details
questions.explain: The course describes exam format qualitatively — proctored, multiple-choice, administered by accredited institutes like PeopleCert — rather than guessing at specifics.
